plan.notes: Sequence transcribed verbatim from the official Anoka-Ramsey Community College 2024-2025 Academic Catalog (archived official catalog), program page 'Professional Nursing Program, AS' (Major Code 5275; https://catalog.anokaramsey.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=2&poid=221, retrieved 2026-10-01). This is the Traditional RN track; the LPN to RN track is a separate plan. Semester totals print as 16 / 17 / 16 / 15 = 64 credits, matching the catalog's Total Credits: 64 (34 nursing + 30 general education). CURRENCY CAVEAT: the school has since published newer official curriculum plans — 'Nursing Curriculum Plan for LPNs (starting with application to the Fall 2025 term)' and 'Nursing Curriculum Plan for RNs (starting Fall 2026)' — whose course credits appear to differ from this 2024-2025 catalog for some courses (notably NURS 1262, NURS 2462, and the PSYC 1110/2235 options), but those PDFs' two-column text extraction is too garbled to decode individual course credits reliably, so they could not be transcribed. This plan is therefore labeled with its actual catalog year (2024-2025) and should be re-verified against the current catalog before being treated as the current plan. Completion requirements per the catalog: minimum 64 semester credits in courses numbered 1000+, 2.0 cumulative GPA at ARCC, grade of C or higher in all program and specified general education requirements, 'safe professional practice' evaluation in clinicals, all NURS courses in each semester completed concurrently with C or higher to progress, general education courses may be taken earlier but not later than the identified semester, nursing courses must be completed within 3 years. The program is a dual-admission (DAP) pathway with Metropolitan State University and Minnesota State University Moorhead; semesters 5-8 (BSN) are completed at the partner university, not at ARCC, and are not part of this 64-credit AS plan. Lab/clinical contact-hour breakdowns printed in the catalog (e.g., NURS 1290: 1 lab + 2 clinical) are not encoded per course; see the catalog program page. Prerequisite annotations transcribed verbatim from the official catalog; "or" alternatives (e.g. BIOL 1900 or BIOL 2201) preserved as one_of. Codes in external_prereqs are catalog-listed alternatives to in-plan courses, satisfied outside this plan's sequence.
